content_html:
When traveling to Peru, having mobile internet can make your trip much easier. It allows you to use maps, request transportation, communicate with hotels or travel agencies, and share your experiences in real time. Fortunately, there are several SIM and internet options for tourists that are affordable and easy to obtain.

Buying a Local SIM Card in Peru

One of the most common ways to access mobile internet is to buy a prepaid SIM card from a local operator. These SIM cards work with most unlocked smartphones.

Main mobile operators in Peru

  • Claro
  • Movistar
  • Entel
  • Bitel

These companies offer prepaid plans with mobile data, calls, and text messages at affordable prices.

Approximate prices

SIM card: free or between $1 and $3 USD

Data packages:

  • 3 to 5 GB: $5 – $8 USD
  • 10 GB: $10 – $15 USD
  • 20 GB or more: $15 – $25 USD

You can buy SIM cards at:

  • Airports
  • Shopping malls
  • Official mobile operator stores
  • Small kiosks or local shops

Using an eSIM for Travel in Peru

If your phone supports eSIM, this is one of the most convenient options for tourists.

With an eSIM, you can activate mobile data before arriving in Peru, without needing to change your physical SIM card.

Advantages of eSIM

Instant activation
No need to look for a store
Keep your main phone number active

Plans usually cost between $8 and $30 USD, depending on the amount of data included.

Wi-Fi in Hotels, Cafés, and Restaurants

In major tourist cities such as Cusco, Lima, and Arequipa, most:

  • Hotels
  • Restaurants
  • Cafés
  • Airports

offer free Wi-Fi for customers.

However, in rural areas or during excursions such as Machu Picchu, Rainbow Mountain, or the Sacred Valley, internet signal may be limited.

Which Operator Has the Best Coverage?

In general:

  • Claro → Good nationwide coverage
  • Movistar → Good speed in cities
  • Entel → Excellent mobile data speed
  • Bitel → Budget-friendly and good signal in some rural areas

In popular tourist destinations like Cusco and the Sacred Valley, Claro and Entel usually provide the best coverage.
